steps: Open the prepared nine-binding source. No copy target is selected automatically. Selecting a named crystal changes neither the form nor any author byte; three-language 390px views preserve the choice.

Explicitly copy the current unfinished numeric row and signal mapping. The new binding has its own identity and selected target, keeps the incomplete input and resets target selection. Review refuses the number without losing input; Cancel and reopen restore all original author bytes and nine bindings.

Recreate the missing second and third crystal bindings by explicit target choices and two fresh identities. Copy revokes review; target selection alone preserves it. Cleared targets prevent duplicate clicks, an old reference control cannot fill a copied row, and review/apply write no author file. Ordinary Save changes only the behavior source while preserving all nine original binding byte ranges and BOM/CRLF.

Reload and reopen the saved manifest: both new identities and explicit crystal targets survive, the four-scene assembly has a valid eleven-binding level, and the retained author-final copy exactly matches all saved author files for independent native gameplay verification.

The fixture removes two existing collection bindings and gives the remaining manifest BOM/CRLF and equivalent JSON spellings. The UI recreates those bindings with fresh identities and explicit instance choices; no runtime or script source is patched.
Scratch numeric input and a signal mapping are used only in the canceled form. They are not saved, do not claim script export discovery and are absent from the final runnable author workspace.

A detached old reference control is dispatched after copying to another binding. No catalog result is fabricated. This check records browser authoring and a valid saved assembly plan; native gameplay is verified separately.
